description: Defaults for unattended runs. The owner overrides any of them once with `softory charter approve <file>` at a terminal; the result lives in local.json. Agents read it with `softory charter show` and never change it.

environment.description: What agents can reach, as the owner declares it. Softory never enforces it; the harness does. Planning and the feasibility check read it, so a plan that needs more becomes a provisioning request instead of a stuck task.

decisions.description: Every escalation names a recommended option and whether it can be undone. One that can be undone applies after default_after_hours with no answer, as a decision the owner can reverse with softory answer; one that can't waits. With quinn_settles, Quinn splits, drops, or allows one more round on a unit at the review cap (one extra round per unit); the owner sees it in the digest.

feasibility.description: Before a story's tasks start, a fresh Quinn run on a different model reads the plan, the charter, and the environment and records pass or what's missing. With required, todo tasks under a story wait for a pass.

design.description: The design standard's machine gates. With wait_for_design, a todo ui or frontend task under a story whose lane:design task isn't done waits: its builder isn't woken, and queue says why. With detect, and the impeccable skill installed, softory verify on a ui unit also scans the unit's own UI files with Impeccable's detector; error and warning findings fail the verify, advisory ones are counted. Exceptions live in .impeccable/config.json, each with a reason.

epics.description: Epics inside these limits start without the owner's go/no-go. Greg raises an escalation to the owner for anything bigger.

budget.description: Caps per role per day, in runs and minutes, so they hold whatever the model costs. Set for Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; tune after a week of softory usage. The usd caps are off at 0; usd_per_run is enforced by Claude Code itself, and the daily usd cap counts the cost each run reports. roles overrides any cap for one role.

task_caps.description: A unit with review_rounds requests for changes stops and goes to the owner. Review records never count, and up to free_evidence_rounds requests whose every item is labelled evidence: are free.

waste.description: The digest flags an open unit whose record changed this many times without closing (claims, status moves, retags), a sign a role is looping on tooling instead of the work. 0 turns it off.

simplify.description: Sage keeps the delivery process simple. role checks in at most every checkin_hours, and only when the team ran, filed feedback, or left clutter since the last check-in; each check-in measures with softory flow --record. process_paths are files that change how work is built or delivered: a unit that changes one needs the process tag, so Sage reviews it. With clean_handoff, softory handoff refuses while untracked files that appeared during the claim sit in the main checkout.

review_batch.description: Wake a reviewer once this many reviews wait, or once the oldest has waited this long, so one run clears several. Reviews also wait until softory verify passes at the commit.

verify.description: softory verify runs command at the unit's commit, one at a time per project. setup, when set, runs first and its failure is a setup failure, not a test failure. share lists folders from the main checkout to bring in, cloned copy-on-write (share_mode clone) so an installer can't delete them; link is the 0.4 behaviour. keep lists globs copied out of the tree when a run fails.

permissions.description: Claude Code runs each role with a settings file built from these and its lane paths. Commands are prefixes.

effort.description: Reasoning effort by kind of run: review when a role only has reviews, closes, or messages waiting, otherwise build. models.<role>.effort overrides it for one role.

prices.description: USD per million tokens, used only when a harness reports tokens but no cost (Codex). Check them against your plan.

models.description: Per role: the default harness and model, and an optional stronger one used once a task has had escalate_model_after rounds of requested changes. Chosen on 2026-10-24 from benchmarks that fit each role's work; see docs/models.md. also lists other harnesses the owner lets the role start on (softory start refuses the rest).
